headline: ESPR and right-to-repair developments increase operational demands on brand importers
summary: New technical standards for Digital Product Passports and right-to-repair clarifications reinforce importer duties for power tools and garden equipment. Concurrently, pushback against weakening CSRD non-EU requirements underscores the need to maintain rigorous supplier ESG data collection in China.

items.title: EU Right-to-Repair rules clarify importer and distributor liabilities
items.what: Industry reporting highlighted that upcoming EU Right-to-Repair rules place direct obligations on importers to ensure product reparability and spare part access.
items.meaning: As the brand owner and importer, you bear direct legal responsibility for repair access, repair documentation, and parts availability for imported power tools.
items.action: Review spare parts stocking arrangements and repair manual data flows with Chinese manufacturing partners.

sources.title: EU Right-to-Repair Rules Put Importers And Distributors On The Hook

items.title: Standards established for Digital Product Passport data security under ESPR
items.what: Two new European standards were developed addressing data security and access control architecture for Digital Product Passports under ESPR.
items.meaning: Technical frameworks for DPP are taking shape, requiring secure systems to intake component and circularity data from Chinese suppliers.
items.action: Assess supplier data systems against emerging DPP security and access standards.

sources.title: Digital Product Passport: Two New EU Standards for Data Security and Access Control

items.title: Stakeholders resist proposed CSRD reporting reliefs for non-EU companies
items.what: Investors and sustainable finance groups voiced strong opposition against proposed relaxations of CSRD sustainability reporting rules for non-EU entities.
items.meaning: Expectations for comprehensive supply-chain disclosure remain high; reporting reliefs for non-EU supply chains are unlikely to reduce your upstream diligence burden.
items.action: Continue onboarding Chinese suppliers onto auditable greenhouse gas and labour data templates.

sources.title: Scepticism mounts over non-EU reporting reliefs under CSRD
Sustainable Finance and Investor Groups Push Back Against Weaker CSRD Sustainability Reporting Rules for Non-EU Companies

items.title: Industry pilots battery passport ahead of EU Battery Regulation deadlines
items.what: Jinko ESS initiated a battery passport pilot with the Global Battery Alliance to test compliance with EU Battery Regulation data requirements.
items.meaning: Validates technical mechanisms for battery passports ahead of February 2027 deadlines, directly relevant to your proprietary battery platform.
items.action: Engage battery cell suppliers to benchmark their data readiness against GBA passport criteria.

sources.title: Jinko ESS Pilots Battery Passport with the Global Battery Alliance, Accelerating Compliance with the EU Battery Regulation

items.title: ESMA proposes narrower metrics to simplify EU Taxonomy reporting
items.what: ESMA proposed narrowing disclosure metrics to reduce compliance burdens and streamline EU Taxonomy reporting for non-financial undertakings.
items.meaning: As an EU-listed company in scope of Taxonomy reporting, future disclosure requirements may become less complex if the Commission endorses the proposal.
items.action: Track whether the European Commission adopts ESMA's proposed reporting simplifications.

sources.title: ESMA proposes simpler EU Taxonomy reporting to reduce compliance burdens
ESMA proposes simpler EU Taxonomy reporting rules
ESMA Proposes Narrower Metrics for EU Taxonomy Disclosure Rules
